name: API Evangelist tool role vocabulary
description: What a tool DOES to a specification. An agent holding an artifact and a goal resolves to a role, and from the role to a shortlist of tools, without reading prose.

authors.question: Where does the artifact itself come from?
authors.returns: The specification document, or the editing surface that produces one.
authors.agent_note: An `authors` tool is usually the spec repository or a visual editor. An agent rarely invokes it; it reads it to learn what the current version actually says.

parses.question: Turn this document into a structure I can traverse.
parses.returns: An in-memory model, AST or resolved document with $refs followed.
parses.agent_note: The right first call when the agent needs to REASON about a contract rather than display it. Resolution of external $refs is where most agent pipelines break.

validates.question: Is this document correct, and does it meet our rules?
validates.returns: A pass/fail plus a list of findings with locations.
validates.agent_note: The highest-value role for an agent, because the output is machine-readable and falsifiable. Distinguish spec-validity (is this legal OpenAPI?) from style-governance (does it meet OUR rules?) — Spectral and vacuum do both, most validators only the first.

tests.question: Does the running implementation match the document?
tests.returns: Contract-test results — where the deployed API and its description disagree.
tests.agent_note: This is the role that catches the failure a document alone cannot: an accurate spec describing an API that no longer behaves that way.

scans.question: What known problems are present in this artifact?
scans.returns: Findings keyed to an identifier — a CVE, an OSV id, a rule.
scans.agent_note: Output is usually already in a standard schema, so it composes without parsing prose.

generates.question: Produce code or artifacts from this document.
generates.returns: SDKs, server stubs, types, documentation, or an SBOM.
generates.agent_note: Check `produces:` for what specifically comes out. Generation is the role most often run in CI, so an agent proposing it should expect to touch a pipeline, not just a file.

transforms.question: Change this document without forking it.
transforms.returns: A modified document, ideally by a declared, replayable change.
transforms.agent_note: The role agents should prefer over hand-editing. An Overlay is a reviewable diff against a contract the agent does not own; a hand edit is an unreviewable fork.

converts.question: Move this between formats or versions.
converts.returns: The same description expressed in another specification or version.

encodes.question: Read and write this format on the wire.
encodes.returns: A serialized message, or a parsed one.
encodes.agent_note: Almost always a language SDK. Pick by the runtime the agent is already in.

serves.question: Stand up an implementation of this specification.
serves.returns: A running server, control plane, or runtime.

mocks.question: Give me a working endpoint before the real one exists.
mocks.returns: A live server that answers per the description.
mocks.agent_note: The safest way for an agent to exercise an integration end to end without credentials, cost, or side effects on a production system.

proxies.question: Sit in the request path and enforce something.
proxies.returns: A gateway or proxy configured from the specification.

runs.question: Execute the artifact.
runs.returns: A running workload — a container started from an image, or the executed steps of a workflow document with what each call actually returned.
runs.agent_note: The role that separates description from proof. A `validates` tool tells you the document is well-formed; a `runs` tool makes the real calls, with real credentials and real side effects. Check `mutates` and `credentials` before invoking one.

deploys.question: Install and manage this in a cluster.

scrapes.question: Collect this data on an interval and store it.
scrapes.returns: A time series database with the collected series.

instruments.question: Emit this data from my application.
instruments.returns: A library or agent that produces conformant telemetry.

signs.question: Attach a verifiable signature to this artifact.
signs.returns: A signature, bundle, or signed envelope.

verifies.question: Should I trust this artifact?
verifies.returns: A trust decision plus the evidence behind it.
verifies.agent_note: The role that matters most when an agent is about to CONSUME something it did not build. An agent installing an unverified artifact is the supply-chain attack.

attests.question: Record a claim about how this artifact was produced.
attests.returns: An attestation — a signed statement with a predicate.

issues.question: Mint an identity or credential for a workload.

evaluates.question: Resolve this flag or policy for the current context.
evaluates.returns: A decision — a flag value or a policy result.

stores.question: Where does this artifact live so others can retrieve it?

transfers.question: Move this artifact between registries or to disk.
transfers.returns: The artifact, moved or inspected, usually without a daemon.
transfers.agent_note: Daemonless transfer tools are the ones that actually work inside an agent sandbox, where there is no container runtime to talk to.

documents.question: Render this document for a human.
documents.returns: Reference documentation, a portal, or an interactive console.
documents.agent_note: Lowest agent value per se — but an agent asked to "improve the developer experience" is usually being asked for this, and it is what a human reviewer will look at.

manages.question: Give an operator a surface to administer this.

produces.sdk: A client library in a target language.
produces.client: A typed caller for the described API.
produces.server-stub: Scaffolding that implements the described interface.
produces.types: Type definitions only — no transport, no runtime.
